title: Fuel pressure and leak-down test (fuel injected)
tools: Fuel pressure gauge kit with Schrader adapter
warnings: Fire risk: no sparks, have an extinguisher close
Direct-injection high-pressure systems (thousands of psi) cannot be tested with a standard gauge. Use scan-tool data.
steps: Find the test port (Schrader valve on the fuel rail). If there is none, an inline adapter is needed.
Wrap the port with a rag and connect the gauge.
Key on (engine off) to prime. Read pressure and compare to spec for the system (port-injected systems commonly run about 35-65 psi; throttle-body systems much lower).
Start and idle. On return-style systems, pulling the regulator vacuum hose should raise pressure roughly 5-10 psi.
Snap the throttle; pressure should hold steady, not drop away.
Shut off and watch the gauge. It should hold most of its pressure for several minutes. Fast drop = leaking injector, regulator or pump check valve.
Low pressure: check the filter, then pump voltage and ground at the pump connector under load before condemning the pump.
